items.name: Inflect-Micro-v2
items.summary: A 9.36M-parameter speech model praised for its unusually small footprint.
items.why_included: A developer replaced an older ONNX model and called its quality amazing.
items.evidence: HN commenter modinfo directly praised it after replacing an older ONNX model.

evidence_sources.author: modinfo
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is amazing, the quality blow my mind for such small model! I just replaced my old onnx model with yours! here my implementation with speech dispatcher and server: https://github.com/skorotkiewicz/inflect-speechd thanks for shearing!

items.name: Milk-V Duo
items.source_story_title: Running a 28.9M parameter LLM on an $8 microcontroller
items.summary: Low-cost Linux-capable RISC-V boards with optional TPU acceleration.
items.why_included: A hands-on user praised the value and bought several.
items.evidence: A commenter highlighted the board's memory, TPU, Linux support, and purchase price.

evidence_sources.author: titzer
evidence_sources.excerpt: It's crazy what $5 can buy you in a microcontroller these days. Have a look at these Milk-V boards: https://milkv.io The duo has up to 256MB of memory, and a 1TOPS@INT8 TPU. They run Linux and are $5. I bought 5!

items.name: htmx
items.source_story_title: Htmx 4.0, the first JavaScript library to release exclusively on the Game Boy
items.summary: A small web library for server-driven dynamic interfaces.
items.why_included: A builder reported replacing OSS apps with simpler htmx-based systems.
items.evidence: A home-server user said htmx replacements were lightweight, responsive, and easy to maintain.

evidence_sources.author: throw2ih020
evidence_sources.excerpt: HTMX is awesome. I've replaced several OSS web apps on my home server with HTMX + Go + PostgreSQL replacements. The results are lightweight, responsive, work great on desktop and mobile alike, all with the absolute minimum complexity required.

items.name: Ruff
items.source_story_title: Ruff v0.16.0 – Significant new updates – 413 default rules up from 59
items.summary: A fast Python linter and formatter with a broadened default rule set.
items.why_included: A user said the upgrade improved code quality and caught new issues.
items.evidence: A maintainer of a 3,000-line project reported useful newly enabled checks.

evidence_sources.author: nickjj
evidence_sources.excerpt: I updated a ~3k line Python project with this the other day. I was using v0.15.x beforehand. It didn't take too long and the new rules do improve code quality. It caught quite a few things previous versions didn't.

items.name: Go Analysis Framework
items.source_story_title: Go Analysis Framework: modular static analysis by go team
items.summary: Go tooling for building modular static analyzers.
items.why_included: A production user reported success defining custom analyzers.
items.evidence: A SpiceDB contributor said their team has had substantial success with custom analyzers.

evidence_sources.author: jzelinskie
evidence_sources.excerpt: For SpiceDB[0], we've found a lot of success using this framework to define our own analyzers; it's probably 10x easier now with LLMs.

items.name: Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos
items.summary: Steven Strogatz’s accessible introduction to nonlinear dynamics and chaos.
items.why_included: It was directly recommended for readers interested in the math.
items.evidence: A commenter called it a great book for the mathematics behind the topic.

evidence_sources.author: milanhbs
evidence_sources.excerpt: For people interested in the related math, "Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos" by Steven Strogatz is a great book! Pdfs abound online.
